## Highlights
### New
- On iPhone and iPad, a floating sidebar has an arrow at its bottom corner that slides it back off the screen.
### Improved
- On iPhone and iPad, scrolling or zooming the page puts a floating sidebar away, as tapping the page already did. - On iPhone, the address bar slides out of the way while you type into a page, such as filling in a form, and comes back when the keyboard goes.
### Fixed
- On iPhone and iPad, History, Archive and Downloads from a keyboard shortcut, the menu bar or the command palette slide a hidden floating sidebar in with that list. A docked iPad sidebar stays docked, and an iPhone showing its tabs full screen opens the list as a sheet instead of doing nothing. - On iPhone and iPad, a tap at the edge of the screen no longer brings out a hidden sidebar; swipe in from the edge instead.
---

## Highlights
### Fixed
- Downloads follow the Automatic Downloads choice of the site you’re on, including files it serves from another address, such as GitHub release files. A blocked download’s message no longer appears twice. - Chromium pages use your default zoom when they open and keep your chosen zoom as you navigate. - Chromium is updated to 154.0.8037.57 with upstream security and compatibility fixes.
